question.text: This city that sits on both sides of the Dnieper ("duh-NEE-per") River is home to the St. Sophia Cathedral and the historic Golden Gate. It is the capital of the Ukraine.
question.clue: A ruler of this city militarily supported the Byzantine emperor Basil II, which resulted in the formation of the Varangian Guard, in exchange for marrying Basil II's sister Anna.

swap.text: This mystic and advisor to Nicholas II avoided being executed along with the imperial family because he had already been poisoned, stabbed, shot, and drowned.

question.text: The Cossack rebel Yemelyan Pugachev claimed to be the dead husband of this "great" Empress of Russia, and launched a rebellion. He was unsuccessful.
question.answerHtml: Catherine the Great [or Catherine II of Russia; or Yekaterina II Velikaya; or Sophie Friederike Auguste, Prinzessin von Anhalt-Zerbst]
question.clue: This ruler's administration saw a rebellion of Yaik Cossacks led by Pugachev and three partitions of Poland.

swap.text: This leader's policies, including glasnost and perestroika, led to the end of the Soviet Union. He was famously implored by Reagan to tear down the Berlin Wall.
swap.clue: This leader, who described his diplomacy with the "Sinatra Doctrine," appointed Eduard Shevardnadze as his Minister of Foreign Affairs and succeeded Constantin Chernenko.

question.leadin: The nurse Darya Mikhailova ("mih-HAIL-oh-vuh") took care of Russian soldiers from this war wounded at the Battle of Alma.
question.text: Name this 1853-1856 war, during which Sevastopol ("seh-VAST-oh-pull") was besieged for eleven months. A group of 38 nurses worked at the Scutari Barracks during this war.
question.clue: This war began after one side issued an ultimatum that asserted its right to protect foreign Christians.

swap.text: Lenin introduced this economic plan that introduced "state capitalism" to the Soviet Union. It abolished forced grain requisition but it also led to the Scissors Crisis when a huge gap between industrial and agricultural prices formed.
swap.clue: This policy's namesake "men" often opened casinos and nightclubs.

question.leadin: Napoleon signed a lot of treaties.
question.text: While on a yacht in the Neman river, Napoleon signed the treaty of Tilsit with this monarch. This czar led Russia during Napoleon's conquests.
question.clue: After his nation lost the Battle of Friedland, he met with Napoleon on a raft in the Niemen River to sign the Treaty of Tilsit.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Rurikid dynasty.
swap.text: The Rurikid dynasty came to an end when Ivan IV was succeeded by Boris Godunov, whose death began this period in Russian history. It was ended by Mikhail Romanov's accession.
swap.clue: Marina Mniszech fought to have her two husbands crowned as Dmitry during this period with the support of Poland-Lithuania.

question.text: The first king of Moscow to assume the title of tsar, he is remembered for acts of cruelty, such as killing his son in an argument, and for subjugating the boyars by creating the oprichnina.
question.answerHtml: Ivan the Terrible [or Ivan IV; or Ivan Vasilyevich; or Ivan Grozny; prompt on Ivan]
question.clue: This ruler allegedly blinded the architect who built him a cathedral and kept nobles in line with his secret police force, the Oprichniki.

swap.leadin: A common Russian joke went, "Stalin proved that just one person could manage the country. [This man] proved that a country doesn't need to be managed at all."
swap.text: Name this long-ruling Soviet leader who sent tanks to quash reforms undertaken by Alexander Dubcek.
swap.clue: His economic policies have been described as "the lowest stage of socialism," and this man is remembered for recognizing postwar European boundaries with the Helsinki Accords.

question.text: This was the name for the Russian nobles who took advantage of beleaguered tsars during the period. Before coming to power, Boris Godunov was one of these people.
question.clue: To undermine the influence of these people, a tsar introduced a system in which collegiate registrars were graded "K-14."

swap.text: This former FSB officer accused his former employer of being the real perpetrator behind the Moscow apartment bombings to garner support for Vladimir Putin. This man was then promptly poisoned with polonium-210 after meeting with two Russian agents at a sushi bar in London.
swap.clue: Shortly before that, he appeared in a video tape revealing other orders to kidnap and kill, and he had been arrested earlier for theft of explosives and abuse of office in Kostroma.

question.leadin: Originally sharing the monarchy with his sickly half brother, Ivan V, he modernized Russia and eventually removed his half-sister Sophia from power.
question.text: This is what Russian Tzar who fought the great Northern war against Charles XII of Sweden?
question.answer: Peter I or Peter the Great
question.clue: This ruler tortured a son named Alexei who died in jail.

swap.leadin: This man taught graduate courses at Stanford's Hoover Institute after his exile.
swap.text: Name this man who led a provisional government that was opposed during the July Days protests. This former member of the Duma served as the effective leader of his country until the October Revolution.
swap.clue: A July 1917 operation named for this man was the last Russian offensive in World War One, commanded by Aleksei Brusilov.

question.leadin: Name these people involved in the end of the Romanov dynasty.
question.text: Following the Kornilov Affair, this man assumed the role of commander in chief of Russian armed forces and proclaimed a republic, but he was deposed in the October Revolution.
question.clue: One leader of the February Revolution was this Prime Minister of the provisional government, who launched a namesake offensive against Austria-Hungary and Germany before being deposed by Lenin in the October Revolution.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about heroic Soviet urban renaming practices.
swap.text: Volgograd was the site of one of the bloodiest battles in human history, lasting from August 1942 to February 1943, when it was known by this name
swap.clue: In a battle for this city, Operation Uranus resulted in the encirclement of the German Sixth Army under field marshal Friedrich Paulus, which Adolf Hitler then ordered to be supplied from the air.

question.leadin: It's not Frankfurt, but this city was designed by Ernst May and based partially on Gary, Indiana.
question.text: Identify this city located next to a giant iron mountain in the southern Urals.
question.clue: This closed Soviet city that was transformed into an industrial complex based on designs by the American firm Arthur G. McKee and Co., effectively serving as the planned crown jewel of the first Five-Year Plan.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Russian leaders during the Time of Troubles.
swap.text: This powerful regent controlled Russia during the reign of Tsar Feodor the Bellringer. He later got himself elected Tsar by the zemsky sobor and ruled until his death in 1605.
swap.clue: He promoted his friend the Metropolitan Job, thus resulting in the creation of the Patriarchate, and Job would later convene the comission that made this man tsar.

question.text: This Ukrainian anarchist incorporated his eponymous followers in to his Black Cross army, which initially allied with the Bolsheviks against the White Army, but soon turned against Bolshevik oppression and fought against them as well.
question.clue: This leader who invented a horse-drawn open wagon used for drive-by shootings called the tachanka. Late in life, this leader teamed up with August Kork in the Northern Taurida Operation.

swap.text: The "green army" is the name sometimes given to Aleksandr Antonov's forces during this rebellion. This peasant rebellion took place during the Russian Civil War and was ended by Mikhail Tukhachevsky.
swap.clue: This rebellion, which was suppressed with a force of one hundred thousand Red Army troops under Mikhail Tukhachevsky, who used tactics like firing poisonous gas at peasant strongholds.
